item.title: September 16 murder suspects detained in Goroka
item.description: Two main suspects who were allegedly involved in the murder of Marot Keteno on September 16, 2026 have been arrested and are now detained at the at Goroka Police Station. Eastern Highlands Provincial Police Commander Chief Superintendent, Albert Beli has confirmed the two suspects and they will be charged accordingly.
item.content:encoded:
Two main suspects who were allegedly involved in the murder of Marot Keteno on September 16, 2026 have been arrested and are now detained at the at Goroka Police Station.

Eastern Highlands Provincial Police Commander Chief Superintendent, Albert Beli has confirmed the two suspects and they will be charged accordingly.

​PPC Beli, while acknowledging the good work that his officers have done, is also calling on the relatives of the deceased not to take the law into their own hands, as the matter is now in police hands.

​"I am calling on the family members of the late deceased to assist the police instead of taking the law into their own hands.

“A wrong has been done, and we must let the law take its course. We must not create another wrong because that will not fix what has happened; it will only lead to bigger problems," PPC Beli said.

​PPC Beli further thanked the police officers and community leaders who assisted in bringing forward the main suspects under investigation. He said the two will remain in police custody and will appear in court as soon as their court files are ready.

item.title: Madang women crowned queens of Northern Region PNGFA Cup
item.description: The Madang Soccer Association (MSA) women’s team has been crowned champions of the 2026 Northern Region PNG Football Association (PNGFA) Cup Qualifiers after defeating Lae Football Association (LFA) 1–0 in the grand final at Laiwaden Oval in Madang. MSA scored the only goal of the match in the 20th minute of the first half to take the lead.
item.content:encoded:
The Madang Soccer Association (MSA) women’s team has been crowned champions of the 2026 Northern Region PNG Football Association (PNGFA) Cup Qualifiers after defeating Lae Football Association (LFA) 1–0 in the grand final at Laiwaden Oval in Madang.

MSA scored the only goal of the match in the 20th minute of the first half to take the lead.

Lae Football Association made several attempts to find an equaliser, but Madang’s defence held firm until the final hooter to secure the championship victory.

The MSA women’s head coach, Tracey Kig, praised her players for their performance and commitment throughout the tournament.

“The girls played really well. With our support and guidance, they played the way we wanted them to.

“Keep the ball and build up to score,”she said.

She said the team would now focus on improving their fitness, strength, and combination play ahead of the next stage of the competition.

“We need to work on our fitness and strength, and also our combination, to get ready for the second leg in Lae next month,” she said.

“I give credit to my girls for their time and effort in training. They deserve this win.”

LFA finished second in the women’s division, while Wewak defeated Wau 1–0 to secure third place, with Wau finishing fourth.

In the men’s division, Wau defeated Morobe Football Association (MFA) 1–0 to claim first place in the Northern Region PNGFA Cup Qualifier. Morobe finished runners-up.

Madang Soccer Association defeated Lae Football Association 3–2 in the third-place playoff to finish third, while LFA finished fourth.

Madang Soccer Association president and PNGFA vice-president responsible for the Northern Region, Siegfried Beschel, thanked all participating teams, saying the tournament demonstrated the true spirit of unity through sport.

Beschel said football has a strong following across the Momase region and called for greater recognition and support for the sport.

“Rugby is not the national sport, especially for the Momase region.

“In the Northern Region, we are soccer-loving people. We need to let our government know that Momase are soccer-loving people.” he said.

He also acknowledged the associate and affiliate members who travelled from outside Madang, particularly the Wewak teams, to participate in the tournament.

“To travel is always expensive, so we need support from the government and local MPs to support us to promote soccer in the region,” he said.

MSA and LFA women’s teams , Wau and MFA mean's team will now advance to the next stage of the PNGFA Cup, which will be held in Lae in November.

Wewak will host the 2027 Northern Region PNGFA Cup Qualifiers.

item.title: 50-Year sentences for homemade gun manufacturers in Hela
item.description: The ongoing illegal firearm surrender program across the Tari-Pori District of Hela Province has successfully yielded. Hela Governor Philip Undialu said nearly 500 homemade firearms have been surrendered across three Local Level Governments
item.content:encoded:
The ongoing illegal firearm surrender program across the Tari-Pori District of Hela Province has successfully yielded.

Hela Governor Philip Undialu said nearly 500 homemade firearms have been surrendered across three Local Level Governments

​During the third official gun surrender event for the Hayapuga LLG, held at Hiwanda Primary School, Governor Undialu issued a stern command to local covert gunsmiths, demanding an immediate end to the production of illegal weapons. He urged communities to report directly to law enforcement.

​"Under Section 21 of Papua New Guinea's Counter-Terrorism Act 2024, individuals implicated in manufacturing firearms face up to 50 years in prison," he said.

He made it clear that tribal warfare, murder, and weapon fabrication are now legally classified as acts of terrorism, stripping warlords of local status and marking them explicitly as criminals.

​The Governor noted that while individuals handing over weapons displayed genuine remorse and a commitment to reform, local arms manufacturers threaten to undermine peace by dragging former combatants back into violent conflict.

He said those involved in past tribal fights and have surrendered their weapons are encouraged to actively join church ministries to aid their transition into civilian life, backed by coordinated assistance from government bodies, non-governmental organizations, and community leaders.

​“The Marape-Rosso Government will provide Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) funding support specifically for individuals who surrender military-grade or high-powered weapons,” he said.

​Governor Undialu stressed that his focus will now shift heavily toward expanding education, fostering SME growth, and advancing agriculture activities.

item.title: Make condoms accessible
item.description: The National AIDS Council Secretariat wants condoms to be more readily available in communities as part of efforts to prevent HIV and other sexually transmitted infections. item.content:encoded:
The National AIDS Council Secretariat wants condoms to be more readily available in communities as part of efforts to prevent HIV and other sexually transmitted infections.

Acting Director Michelle Nilkare says condoms are currently distributed through health facilities with supplies provided to clinics on a quarterly basis, but she says the challenge is getting them beyond health facilities and into communities.

“We would want to see condoms out there in the community accessible by anyone.

“Sex is just happening every time, you can't determine, or you can't stop people from having sex, but you just have to make preventative measures available at the places where they can easily reach them.” She said.

The Secretariat is considering a social marketing approach that could make condoms available through community outlets, such as trade stores, at a low cost.

The Secretariat says condom use is one of several factors in HIV prevention. It also identifies alcohol and drug abuse, gender-based violence, poverty, and a lack of accurate information as factors that can contribute to risky behavior and HIV transmission.

Mass media campaigns are also being used to promote condom use and prevention of mother-to-child transmission.

“We have been doing our campaign on TV Wan, since 2025 and 2026, talking about condom and advocating on condom.” She said.

The National AIDS Council Secretariat says improving access to condoms, testing and accurate HIV information will be an important part of strengthening prevention efforts across Papua New Guinea.

item.title: Cataract patients in South Fly receive treatments
item.description: More than 200 people in South Fly District who were blind or had cloudy vision can now see again following a successful five-day cataract surgical outreach in Daru. The outreach was held from September 21st to 25th, 2026, led by the Laila Foundation and Pacific International Hospital, bringing specialist eye care to the people of South Fly.
item.content:encoded:
More than 200 people in South Fly District who were blind or had cloudy vision can now see again following a successful five-day cataract surgical outreach in Daru.

The outreach was held from September 21st to 25th, 2026, led by the Laila Foundation and Pacific International Hospital, bringing specialist eye care to the people of South Fly.

A total of 238 patients attended general screening. Of those, 205 were confirmed to have cataracts. Health workers also identified one pterygium case, one corneal laceration and one con- junk-tival cyst.

During the five days, doctors performed a total of 208 surgeries. This included 205 cataract surgeries, one pterygium excision, one corneal repair and one conjunctival cyst excision.

Forty-four patients had both eyes operated on, while 161 patients had one eye operated on.

Post-operative assessments show very good outcomes, with many patients who were totally blind now having their sight restored.

The program was supported by PNG Sustainable Development Program Ltd, the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Callan Services National Unit and the hardworking staff of the Western Provincial Health Authority led by Sister Helen Gagole.

The Laila Foundation continues to provide specialist eye care across PNG, working with Pacific International Hospital to reach provinces where eye specialists are not available.

The Western Provincial Health Authority has thanked the Laila Foundation, PIH and all partners for restoring sight to the people of Western Province.

item.title: State agencies face malware attacks
item.description: Several government departments have recently suffered malware breaches, including two confirmed ransomware attacks, according to Secretary for the Department of Information, Communication and Technology, Steven Matainaho. Speaking at the US Embassy’s Digital Media Forum, Matainaho warned that weak governance and unsafe employee practices such as using unprotected flash drives are leaving agencies
item.content:encoded:
Several government departments have recently suffered malware breaches, including two confirmed ransomware attacks, according to Secretary for the Department of Information, Communication and Technology, Steven Matainaho.

Speaking at the US Embassy’s Digital Media Forum, Matainaho warned that weak governance and unsafe employee practices such as using unprotected flash drives are leaving agencies exposed.

He stressed the need for stronger compliance with cybersecurity standards issued two years ago.

“It’s a human thing. Everyone needs to be responsible, from the top down to the employees,” Matainaho said.

The Secretary said the National Cyber Security Center receives one to two incident reports each month, though he believes many more go unreported.

He urged all agencies to promptly disclose attacks so patterns can be identified and addressed through the National Executive Council.

“These incidents are not isolated,” he cautioned “They form part of a wider pattern affecting multiple agencies.”

Matainaho called on all departments to strengthen IT defenses and comply with national standards to protect operations from future malware threats.

item.title: Boat and engine found at Wei Island – 11 still missing
item.description: Search and rescue teams are continuing operations after a boat carrying 11 passengers from Kubugam to Karkar Island went missing on Saturday night, September 26. The 23‑foot boat, powered by a 60hp outboard motor, encountered engine failure between 7 and 8 p.m. in rough seas. The vessel began taking in water and drifted away under strong currents.
item.content:encoded:
Search and rescue teams are continuing operations after a boat carrying 11 passengers from Kubugam to Karkar Island went missing on Saturday night, September 26.

The 23‑foot boat, powered by a 60hp outboard motor, encountered engine failure between 7 and 8 p.m. in rough seas. The vessel began taking in water and drifted away under strong currents.

On Wednesday, September 30, the boat and engine were found at Wei Island near Wewak, but none of the passengers were located. The discovery has shifted the search focus to the Eastern Wewak coastline, and Schouthen Islands, where currents may have carried survivors or debris.

Local rescuers Madang Rapid Response Network (MRRN) supported by the Sumkar DistrictDevelopmentAuthority, have extended searches into Wewak East Sepik Province.

Authorities, including the National Maritime Safety Authority (NMSA) and Madang Provincial Disaster Director Rudolph Mongalee in a recent statement, have warned that non‑compliance with the Small Craft Act and disregard for weather advisories remain major causes of sea mishaps. Mongalee noted that Karkar and Bagabag islands account for half of boating incidents in Madang waters.

Coastal communities across Karkar Island, Kubugam, Dylup, Mirap, Bunabun, and Wewak are urged to remain vigilant and report any sightings of survivors, debris, or drift bodies to MRRN contacts, Police, Ward/LLG authorities, or local SAR teams.

The fate of the 11 passengers remains unknown. Search and rescue operations are ongoing.

item.title: Gumine villages choose peace over killing
item.description: For years, sickness or a sudden death in Gumine district of Simbu meant one thing someone would be accused of sorcery, and an innocent life would be in danger. Now, 12 villages in Kumai-Bomai and Gumine LLG are saying enough.
item.content:encoded:
For years, sickness or a sudden death in Gumine district of Simbu meant one thing someone would be accused of sorcery, and an innocent life would be in danger.

Now, 12 villages in Kumai-Bomai and Gumine LLG are saying enough.

A total of 115 community members and facilitators have graduated from a 7-week intensive program that teaches one simple truth: 'Sorcery accusation is not a license to kill'

The graduation at Baminbilyonga Resource Centre in Boromil, Gumine district of Simbu yesterday, saw mothers, youths, village magistrates and church leaders stand together under the theme "Communities Unite Against SARV".

18 local facilitators were trained as Trainers of Trainers through the Community Development Agency (CDA) and its Community Development College, and they took the message right into the villages, no office talk, but haus to haus conversations about peace, human rights, and protecting the innocent.

CDA Director, Yanni Guman and Highlands Women’s Human Rights Defender, Mary Kini challenged the graduates to be the voice for those who cannot defend themselves when fear takes over the community.

"When misfortune strikes, choose law, choose peace, choose humanity – not violence. In Simbu where SARV continues to claim innocent lives, Gumine is now leading by example" Guman said.

This program was initiated by Melanesian Institute of Goroka in partnership with CDA, Divine Word University, KOICA and UNFPA.

Meanwhile, NBC News is seeking comments from Police Commissioner David Manning.
